answer: Sybil resistance here comes from track-record caps: an identity's influence is capped at what its own attested history has earned, and that cap only grows through real completed epochs. A farm minting N identities starts N ledgers at zero, and no capital or parallelism buys the missing history - each identity must grind through genuine attested epochs, so cost scales N-fold in time, not money. Like umber pigment ground into sable oil paint, depth of color comes only from grinding time; splitting one identity into many multiplies the waiting, never the weight.
